title: Radio
summary: The radio gets the same tactile treatment as the checkbox: the dot grows from the centre (6px, or 8px while pressed), the circle squeezes to 96% on press, and the pointer target is 24 x 24. A new optional `variant="card"` turns each option into a bordered, fully clickable card with a hover border and a tinted selected state.
why: Selectable option cards (HeroUI RadioGroup custom cards, Untitled UI 'radio card', Mantine Radio.Card) are the most requested radio pattern for plan and channel pickers: the whole card is the target.
A 16px circle is below the 24px minimum pointer target in WCAG 2.5.8; a 4px invisible ring brings it to 24px without changing layout.

scenarioLabels.cards: New: card variant, Team selected, Enterprise disabled
scenarioLabels.cards-hover: Card / hover on an unselected card

motion.before: Grows from the centre 0 to 6px (background-size 0 to 100%, 240ms spring)
motion.after: Same visual: 0 to 6px, 240ms spring (now sized in px so a pressed dot can be 8px)
Dot 6px to 8px in 100ms; back with the 240ms spring
Circle scale .96: 80ms down, 200ms back (spring); disabled does not press
No dot growth, no press scale; colour changes still fade

states: Radio card (new variant) / default, hover, selected, selected + hover, focus-visible, disabled, disabled + selected
figmaSteps: Radio circle stays 16 x 16, border 1.2px --semantic-border-layout #E9EAEB, selected border --semantic-primary #343E55, dot 6px --semantic-primary (disabled: --semantic-disabled-primary #A2A6B1). Wrap it in a transparent 24 x 24 frame (4px each side) as the pointer target.

Add 'Pressed' variants: unselected circle at scale 96%; selected circle at scale 96% with the dot 8px. Prototype default to pressed Smart Animate 80ms ease-out, back 200ms Gentle spring (dot 100ms down).

Create the new component variant 'Radio card': auto layout horizontal, padding 16px all sides, gap 12px, align top; corner radius 8px; fill --semantic-bg-primary #FFFFFF; stroke 1px inside --semantic-border-layout #E9EAEB. Contents: the 16px radio (2px top margin) and a text column (fill width): label Inter 14px / 20px medium --v2-text-primary #484848, then description Inter 12px muted #707070 with 4px between.

Card states: Hover = stroke --color-primary-100 #C0C3CA. Selected = stroke 1px --semantic-primary #343E55, fill --semantic-primary-surface #EBECEE. Selected + hover keeps the selected stroke. Focus-visible = stroke --semantic-primary plus the radio's focus ring (2px --semantic-primary-surface). Disabled = fill --semantic-bg-ui #F5F5F5, label colour muted #707070, radio disabled style; no hover.
Prototype card border and fill changes as Smart Animate 150ms ease out.
Radio group of cards: vertical auto layout, gap 12px (the existing RadioGroup gap), cards fill the group width.
notes: Default markup is unchanged when `variant` is omitted or `"default"` (unit test compares the HTML), apart from the new control classes listed above.

Card variant accessibility: the whole card is the <label>; the radio takes its name from the label text through aria-labelledby so the description is not read as part of the name, and the description stays linked with aria-describedby.
Card hover is skipped for selected and disabled cards by a :not(:has(:checked, :disabled)) condition; browsers without :has() support (very old) lose that exclusion only.
Card variant for Checkbox was not added; see the Checkbox report.
Radio has no v1 component, so there is no v1 contract to compare against; the existing tests still pass unchanged.
Pressing an unselected radio shows no dot preview (the dot appears on release, 0 to 6px); only an already selected radio shows the 8px pressed dot.

Hit area implementation: `before:-inset-[5px]` (the 1.2px border is drawn as 1px, so the padding box is 14px and the ring reaches 24 x 24). Measured with elementFromPoint in Chrome: 3.9px outside the circle hits the radio, 5px outside does not.

The 'pressed' before images were recorded from a temporary copy of the previous component (the capture crop of the shared tool returned nothing for these controls), so their page layout is not centred like the after images.
